Browser launch commands for social media operations:

Always run the correct browser command before ANY social media operation. LinkedIn native tools (get_my_profile, etc.) don't need it. Never fail silently; initialize browser first.

Browser MCP account mapping fix: The skill file uses "prateek"/"swastik" but the browser-mcp server reads from ~/.browser-mcp/profiles.json which must match. Updated profiles.json keys from "default"/"a2" to "prateek"/"swastik". Also changed config.py DEFAULT_ACCOUNT from "default" to "prateek". No server restart needed — profiles.json is read per-request.

LinkedIn post creation UI fix: The social_post tool fails on profile pages because it looks for class="start-a-post" which doesn't exist there. On linkedin.com/feed/, the correct flow is: 1) Navigate to /feed/ URL, 2) Find input element with aria-label="Start a post", 3) Clicking it opens a dialog, 4) The editor has div.editor-content.ql-container containing div.ql-editor.ql-blank for text input. Always ensure browser is on linkedin.com/feed/ before attempting social_post.

LinkedIn social_post tool troubleshooting: If "start-a-post button not found", navigate to https://www.linkedin.com/feed/ first (not profile page). The post editor uses aria-label="Start a post" input → clicks open dialog with ql-container/ql-editor classes. After navigation, wait 3-5 seconds before calling social_post.
Verit Analytics LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/verit-analytics/

Duplicate cleanup preference: when choosing which of two duplicate chats to delete, keep the one that is most detailed / highest quality (more assistant chars, more tool calls, more turns, longer span, richer thinking) — NOT simply the latest by timestamp. Use scripts/fetch_conversation.py (--metrics / --list) to compare before deleting.

Conversation quality signals computed by the script include assistant_chars, tool_call_count, user/assistant turns, thinking_chars, distinct models, and session span_seconds
